newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Power distribution priority for S.African govt.
newsitem.headline: Power distribution priority for S.African govt.

text.p: The overhaul of electricity distribution rather than generation is the main priority for government as it studies ways to restructure the industry, Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau said on Monday.
"Our starting point is to look at the distribution point of that industry," said told a pan-African privatisation conference.

"It is imperative that we as a government should make distribution be of the type that will serve both our giant electricity company, which is Eskom, and the municipalities in a manner which won't hinder growth but will lead to growth."
South African Mineral and Energy Affairs Minister Penuell Maduna said on March 7 the cabinet had approved plans for the long-awaited restructuring of the electricity supply industry.

Proposals include the consolidation of the electricity distribution industry into semi-independent regional electricity distributers; the introduction of cost-reflective tariffs, an electrificiation levy and a capped tax.
Maduna said government's plans had the support of major industry players, who understood and accepted the need for electricity transformation.

But the National Union of Mine Workers (NUM) has rejected the recommendations, saying they represent only the views of employers in the industry and that the process of canvassing views had been "secretive".
